definition: authorship and loss of self-extension as the two things a close tie is made of

settled:
Two separate channels feed a bystander's harm when an intimate is taken, and both are read off the facts rather than declared.

The first is authorship. A close intimate holds a large share of the other's welfare and is factually a dominant cause of that life. That is greater responsibility.

The second is loss of self-extension. Losing an intimate destroys part of how the bystander's own life is constituted, a real reduction in their own value stream. That is greater stake of self.

The two come apart, and the separation shows. Common morality mildly deprioritises step-children, which is the signature of one full channel, since a step-parent genuinely raised the child, and one partial one.

For humans I predict the second channel tracks relatedness, about half for a child or a sibling or a parent and a quarter for a grandchild or a niece, because evolution shaped the human utility function that way. That is a prediction about humans rather than a term in the framework.

title: The Two Channels That Make Someone Mine
